RAYMOND

Master Architecture, Product Vision, System Design, Security Model, Evolution Model and Implementation Specification

You are working on a software platform called Raymond.

Treat this document as the authoritative high-level architectural specification for the intended Raymond platform.

Your job is to understand the complete system before implementing anything.

Do not reduce Raymond to a simple MCP server, chatbot, dashboard, content publisher, cloud application, or collection of integrations.

Raymond is intended to become a modular, provider-independent, distributed personal AI control plane that can manage AI, data, applications, communication, infrastructure, devices, workflows, accounts, capabilities, and its own controlled evolution.

The architecture must be designed so that Raymond can start small and evolve into a large distributed system without requiring the Core to be repeatedly rewritten.

---

1. CORE VISION

Raymond's fundamental idea is:

«Raymond owns the control plane. Providers, infrastructure, AI models, data nodes, devices and capabilities are replaceable resources connected to that control plane.»

Raymond must not become permanently dependent on:

- GitHub
- Cloudflare
- OpenAI
- Anthropic
- Gemini
- DeepSeek
- Telegram
- Instagram
- X
- a particular VPS provider
- a particular database
- a particular cloud
- a particular AI model
- a particular mobile device

These are integrations, providers, nodes, or capabilities.

They are not Raymond itself.

The architectural relationship must therefore be:

                    RAYMOND
                 CONTROL PLANE
                       |
       +---------------+----------------+
       |               |                |
   AI PLATFORM     DATA PLATFORM   CAPABILITY PLATFORM
       |               |                |
       +---------------+----------------+
                       |
              PROVIDER / ADAPTER LAYER
                       |
       +---------------+----------------+
       |               |                |
   Cloud/VPS        Services         Devices
   Servers          APIs             Nodes

Never design:

GitHub -> Cloudflare -> Raymond

Design:

Raymond
  |
  +-- Source Providers
  +-- Runtime Providers
  +-- Data Providers
  +-- AI Providers
  +-- Communication Providers
  +-- Device Nodes
  +-- Infrastructure Nodes

---

2. WHAT RAYMOND ULTIMATELY BECOMES

The final target is a system that can:

- understand natural-language commands
- manage projects
- manage AI models
- manage AI providers
- manage multiple AI accounts
- manage cloud accounts
- manage infrastructure
- manage servers
- manage data nodes
- manage devices
- manage communication services
- manage workflows
- manage capabilities
- manage deployments
- manage backups
- perform controlled migrations
- perform failover
- perform recovery
- perform research
- store and retrieve knowledge
- operate with weak or intermittent Internet
- use local AI
- use external AI
- combine multiple AI agents
- add new capabilities through plugins/adapters
- update capabilities safely
- test changes
- canary changes
- rollback failed changes
- audit important operations
- maintain security boundaries
- operate across multiple nodes
- survive provider/node failures
- migrate between infrastructure providers

The final experience should feel like a personal operating/control system for the user's digital environment.

---

3. FUNDAMENTAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES

These principles are mandatory.

3.1 Core Stable

The Core must change rarely.

Security-critical and identity-critical functionality must not be casually modified by plugins or AI agents.

3.2 Capabilities Plugin-Based

New functionality should normally be added through:

- Capability
- Plugin
- Connector
- Adapter
- Provider implementation

rather than modifying the Core.

3.3 UI Contract-Driven

UI must communicate with stable application contracts.

UI must not directly contain business logic or provider-specific behavior.

3.4 Infrastructure Replaceable

Cloudflare, VPS, local servers, dedicated servers, containers and other infrastructure must be replaceable.

3.5 Provider Independence

Provider-specific implementation belongs behind adapters.

3.6 Changes Localized

A change to Telegram must not require changes to Core authorization.

A change to OpenAI must not require changes to the workflow engine.

A change to Cloudflare must not require redesigning Raymond.

3.7 Safe Evolution

Every significant change should support:

- validation
- testing
- security review
- staging
- canary
- health verification
- rollback
- audit

3.8 Data Ownership

Data must remain portable and controlled by Raymond's data architecture.

3.9 AI Is Not Root Authority

AI may:

- analyze
- plan
- propose
- generate
- review
- optimize

AI must not bypass:

- authentication
- authorization
- policy
- approval
- execution controls
- audit

3.10 Fail Closed

Unknown, invalid, expired, unauthorized or unsafe operations must fail closed.

3.11 Performance by Design

Do not create an architecture where every request passes through ten slow services.

Use:

- Fast Path
- Standard Path
- Deep Path

and appropriate caching, local execution, asynchronous processing and queues.

3.12 Minimal Dependency Principle

Use the smallest dependency surface that can safely provide the required capability.

---

4. ARCHITECTURE LAYERS

The target architecture is:

+------------------------------------------------------+
|                       UI LAYER                       |
| Mobile / Web / Command Center / Control Center      |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|            APPLICATION / CONTROL PLANE              |
| Commands / Operations / Tasks / Workflows / Router  |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|                    CORE DOMAIN                      |
| State / Projects / Resources / Lifecycle / Models  |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|              SECURITY / IDENTITY PLANE              |
| Auth / Authorization / Policy / Risk / Approval    |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|                 CAPABILITY PLATFORM                 |
| Plugins / Tools / Connectors / Operations          |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|              PROVIDER / ADAPTER LAYER              |
| AI / Git / Cloud / Communication / Device Adapters |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|           INFRASTRUCTURE / NODE LAYER               |
| Cloud / VPS / Servers / Devices / Containers       |
+------------------------------------------------------+
                         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
|                  DATA / RUNTIME                    |
| DB / Object Storage / Search / AI Runtime / etc.   |
+------------------------------------------------------+

Dependency direction must generally point downward.

Lower layers must not become dependent on UI.

Core must not directly depend on a specific provider implementation.

---

5. RAYMOND CORE

The Core contains the stable concepts that define Raymond.

Core responsibilities include:

- identity references
- resources
- projects
- environments
- operations
- tasks
- execution state
- lifecycle management
- capability references
- provider references
- node references
- policy references
- audit references
- configuration abstractions

Core must not contain hard-coded implementations for individual providers.

---

6. IMMUTABLE, GOVERNED AND DYNAMIC AREAS

Immutable Core

These areas must have extremely strong protection:

- root identity
- security boundary
- authorization model
- approval integrity
- audit integrity
- recovery foundation
- trust establishment
- secret isolation

Governed Core

These may evolve through controlled changes:

- execution engine
- workflow engine
- task engine
- routing
- capability registry
- AI routing
- orchestration

Dynamic Layer

These should be replaceable:

- plugins
- connectors
- provider adapters
- AI models
- workflows
- node configurations
- UI modules
- integrations
- account profiles

---

7. SECURITY PIPELINE

Every meaningful operation must conceptually pass through:

REQUEST
   |
AUTH
   |
AUTHORIZATION
   |
POLICY
   |
RISK CHECK
   |
APPROVAL
   |
EXECUTION
   |
VERIFICATION
   |
AUDIT

Not every low-risk operation necessarily requires interactive human approval, but the architecture must support policy-defined approval requirements.

High-risk operations must be explicitly controlled.

Examples:

- deployment
- deleting data
- changing security policy
- rotating root credentials
- changing infrastructure
- migrating critical services
- changing protected Core components

must not be silently executed.

---

8. IDENTITY

Identity must be separate from provider accounts.

Concepts include:

- Owner
- User
- Service Identity
- Device Identity
- Node Identity
- Instance Identity
- Capability Identity
- Provider Account
- Session
- Credential Reference

Identity must be globally meaningful inside Raymond without being tied to a provider.

---

9. AUTHENTICATION

Support an extensible authentication architecture.

Potential methods include:

- OAuth
- OAuth 2.x / PKCE where applicable
- API credentials
- device authentication
- node certificates
- signed tokens
- short-lived capability tokens
- session credentials

Secrets must never be placed in:

- source code
- Git
- logs
- audit records
- prompts
- frontend bundles
- normal error messages

---

10. AUTHORIZATION

Authorization must operate on:

- identity
- tenant/instance
- capability
- operation
- resource
- environment
- risk
- policy
- context

Example:

User A
  |
  +-- AI Chat       ALLOW
  +-- AI Coding     ALLOW
  +-- GitHub Read   ALLOW
  +-- GitHub Write  DENY
  +-- Deploy        DENY
  +-- Cloudflare    DENY
  +-- Self Modify   DENY

Authorization must be enforced server-side.

Never trust UI restrictions as security controls.

---

11. POLICY ENGINE

Policy must determine:

- whether an operation is allowed
- whether approval is required
- which provider/account may be used
- which node may execute
- which data may be accessed
- which environment may be modified
- which capabilities are available
- quotas and limits
- risk level
- data residency rules
- retention rules

Policy must be independently testable.

---

12. APPROVAL SYSTEM

Approval must be bound to a specific intended operation.

An approval should not be reusable for a materially different operation.

Approval should include concepts such as:

- approval ID
- operation identity
- requested action
- actor
- scope
- resource
- expiration
- status
- policy context
- audit metadata

Expired or mismatched approvals must fail.

---

13. OPERATION MODEL

Every natural-language command should eventually become an explicit Operation.

Conceptually:

Operation
├── Operation ID
├── Actor
├── Tenant / Instance
├── Request
├── Capability
├── Operation Type
├── Resource
├── Environment
├── Risk
├── Policy Decision
├── Approval
├── Execution
├── Verification
├── Result
├── Rollback Information
└── Audit Reference

This creates a common control model across the entire system.

---

14. CAPABILITY PLATFORM

The old concept of a simple Tool Registry should evolve into a broader Capability Registry.

A capability should have:

Capability
├── Identity
├── Version
├── Manifest
├── Operations
├── Permissions
├── Dependencies
├── Security Requirements
├── Resource Requirements
├── Configuration Schema
├── Provider Requirements
├── Health Checks
└── Lifecycle

Examples:

- GitHub capability
- Cloudflare capability
- Telegram capability
- AI capability
- Data Search capability
- Infrastructure capability
- Device capability
- Backup capability
- Deployment capability

---

15. PLUGIN ARCHITECTURE

Adding a new capability should normally follow:

DISCOVER
   ↓
DEFINE CONTRACT
   ↓
IMPLEMENT PLUGIN / ADAPTER
   ↓
STATIC ANALYSIS
   ↓
TEST
   ↓
SECURITY REVIEW
   ↓
STAGING
   ↓
CANARY
   ↓
VERIFY
   ↓
ACTIVATE
   ↓
AUDIT

If activation causes failures:

DETECT
→ DISABLE
→ ROLLBACK
→ VERIFY
→ AUDIT

Plugins must not bypass Core security.

---

16. PROVIDER REGISTRY

Providers are external implementations of capabilities.

Examples:

AI Providers

- OpenAI
- Anthropic
- Google Gemini
- DeepSeek
- Mistral
- Local AI
- future providers

Source Providers

- GitHub
- GitLab
- self-hosted Git
- local repository

Infrastructure Providers

- Cloudflare
- VPS providers
- dedicated servers
- local infrastructure
- future cloud providers

Communication Providers

- Telegram
- Instagram
- X
- email
- SMS
- telephony

The Provider Registry must make these replaceable.

---

17. CONNECTION MANAGEMENT

Raymond must have a first-class Connection model.

A Connection may contain references to:

- provider
- account identity
- authentication method
- secret reference
- scopes
- environment
- status
- last verification
- health
- security metadata

Secret material itself must remain outside the Core data model.

Connection lifecycle:

DISCOVER
→ AUTHENTICATE
→ VERIFY
→ REGISTER
→ HEALTH CHECK
→ READY

---

18. MULTI-ACCOUNT SYSTEM

Raymond must support multiple accounts per provider.

Examples:

OpenAI
├── Account A
├── Account B
└── Account C

GitHub
├── Account A
└── Account B

Cloudflare
├── Account A
├── Account B
└── Account C

The architecture should support:

- account pools
- health
- availability
- capability
- latency
- cost
- environment
- policy
- failover

This is for legitimate redundancy, continuity and capacity management.

Do not design mechanisms intended to evade provider quotas, rate limits or access restrictions.

---

19. ROUTING ENGINE

Routing determines:

Which capability?
Which provider?
Which account?
Which node?
Which model?
Which environment?
Which execution path?

Routing inputs may include:

- capability
- policy
- health
- latency
- cost
- availability
- resource requirements
- privacy
- locality
- data residency
- model quality
- environment
- user preferences

Routing must be replaceable and policy-aware.

---

20. SOURCE REGISTRY

Source code must be independent from GitHub.

Concept:

Source Registry
├── GitHub Repository A
├── GitHub Repository B
├── GitLab
├── Self-hosted Git
├── Local Repository
└── Future Source Providers

The current project may use GitHub, but GitHub is not the architectural root of Raymond.

---

21. RUNTIME PORTABILITY

Runtime must be portable across:

- Cloudflare
- VPS
- dedicated server
- Docker
- local server
- future cloud providers

A provider-specific runtime adapter must isolate infrastructure differences.

---

22. RAYMOND NODE

A Raymond Node is a registered execution/infrastructure endpoint.

Architecture:

RAYMOND MAIN
      |
 SECURE CHANNEL
      |
 RAYMOND NODE
      |
 OS / CONTAINER / RUNTIME

Node Registry should track:

- node ID
- identity
- version
- status
- health
- heartbeat
- capabilities
- resources
- security state
- environment
- role
- location metadata where appropriate

Node roles may include:

- Compute
- AI
- Data
- Search
- Storage
- Backup
- Build
- Deployment
- Monitoring

---

23. DISTRIBUTED ARCHITECTURE

Raymond must support:

1 Node
↓
2 Nodes
↓
10 Nodes
↓
Many Nodes

without rewriting the Core.

Distributed functionality should eventually include:

- node discovery
- registration
- secure identity
- health
- heartbeat
- replication
- synchronization
- event ordering
- conflict resolution
- versioning
- failover
- migration
- recovery

---

24. FAILURE MODEL

A single failure must not destroy Raymond.

Examples:

GitHub fails

Raymond continues operating.

Cloudflare fails

Raymond can use another runtime when configured.

VPS-01 fails

Raymond can fail over to VPS-02.

AI provider fails

Router can select another configured provider/model.

Data node fails

Replica/recovery mechanisms should preserve data.

Internet becomes unreliable

Local capabilities, queues and offline state continue where policy permits.

---

25. DATA PLATFORM

Raymond requires a separate:

Distributed Data Intelligence Platform

Its responsibility is data infrastructure, not general authority.

The Data Platform may contain:

- raw storage
- structured databases
- full-text search
- semantic/vector search
- metadata
- knowledge graph
- research jobs
- ingestion pipelines
- classification
- deduplication
- entity extraction
- tagging
- indexing
- transcription
- provenance
- backup
- replication
- migration

---

26. DATA OWNERSHIP MODEL

Important principle:

«The Data Node owns data infrastructure. Raymond Main owns authority to access it.»

AI must not automatically receive:

- database administrator access
- raw storage access
- master encryption keys
- unrestricted export access
- unrestricted deletion rights

Example AI permissions:

Search                  ALLOW
Semantic Search         ALLOW
Metadata                ALLOW
Raw Database Access     DENY
Delete                  DENY
Modify                  DENY
Export                  DENY
Admin                   DENY

unless explicitly authorized.

---

27. DATA PROVENANCE

Collected information should track:

- source
- URL where applicable
- timestamp
- collection method
- permissions/context
- classification
- confidence
- processing history
- transformation history

---

28. ENCRYPTION

Use strong encryption architecture.

Prefer:

- envelope encryption
- per-dataset or per-collection data keys
- protected root hierarchy
- KMS/HSM-backed key management where available
- short-lived key-release authorization

Raymond Main should not casually expose master keys to Data Nodes or AI agents.

---

29. DATA MIGRATION

Migration must be a controlled workflow:

DISCOVER
→ SNAPSHOT
→ ENCRYPT
→ PREPARE
→ TRANSFER
→ RESTORE
→ VERIFY
→ REBUILD INDEX
→ HEALTH CHECK
→ SYNC
→ CUTOVER
→ DRAIN OLD NODE
→ REVOKE

Verification should use integrity checks/hashes and application-level health checks.

---

30. DATA PORTABILITY

Data should be exportable as a structured migration package containing, where applicable:

- encrypted data
- metadata
- schema
- index manifest
- integrity hashes
- migration manifest
- configuration references
- provenance metadata

The format must be designed for future infrastructure changes.

36. OFFLINE AND WEAK INTERNET

Raymond must support degraded operation.

Architecture should include:

- local state
- local AI
- queues
- retry
- delta synchronization
- conflict resolution
- cached configuration
- offline authorization leases where appropriate
- local execution
- deferred execution

High-risk actions may require live authority.

Low-risk predefined actions may operate under explicitly configured offline policies.

---

37. PERFORMANCE MODEL

Use three execution paths.

Fast Path

For simple low-risk operations:

Request
→ Auth
→ Policy
→ Local/Direct Execution
→ Result

Standard Path

For normal operations:

Request
→ Auth
→ Authorization
→ Policy
→ Capability
→ Provider
→ Execution
→ Audit

Deep Path

For complex operations:

Request
→ Planning
→ Multiple Agents
→ Review
→ Policy
→ Approval
→ Execution
→ Verification
→ Audit

Do not force every request through Deep Path.

Use:

- caching
- lazy loading
- local execution
- asynchronous jobs
- queues
- delta sync
- connection pooling
- background processing
- minimal dependencies

---

38. CONNECTIVITY SUBSYSTEM

        |

        |

        |

The system may test configured routes, select healthy routes and reconnect automatically.

It must not be designed as an unrestricted mechanism for bypassing access controls or provider restrictions.

41. TELEGRAM

A custom Telegram workspace may use Telegram's TDLib where appropriate.

TDLib is an official Telegram client library designed for custom Telegram applications and handles networking, encryption, local storage and synchronization details.

Do not assume every Telegram feature is automatically available simply because TDLib exists.

Respect Telegram's APIs, policies and account restrictions.

42. INSTAGRAM AND X

44. MOBILE ARCHITECTURE

Raymond Mobile is:

Secure Thin Client + Device Node

It is not the primary storage location for Raymond.

Principle:

«Data belongs to Raymond, not the device.»

The mobile client should keep persistent local state minimal.

Potential persistent data:

- device identity
- session keys
- minimal encrypted cache
- required configuration

Sensitive information should preferably be decrypted only when needed and not unnecessarily persisted.

77. CURRENT BOOTSTRAP ARCHITECTURE

The current project began as:

content-publisher-mcp

The initial purpose was to connect:

ChatGPT
→ MCP Server
→ Cloudflare Worker
→ external publishing services

That was the starting point.

It is not the final architecture.

The project has evolved into Raymond.

The original publishing capability should now be treated as one possible capability inside the broader system.

---

78. CURRENT TECHNOLOGY POSITION

Cloudflare may currently be used as a runtime/infrastructure layer.

Cloudflare Workers currently provides multiple primitives relevant to this architecture, including Workers, D1, R2, Durable Objects, Queues, Vectorize and related services. Durable Objects are particularly relevant for stateful coordination and strongly consistent per-object state, while D1 is suited to relational application data and Queues to asynchronous/background work.

However:

«Cloudflare is an implementation provider, not the Raymond architecture.»

Any Cloudflare-specific implementation must remain behind infrastructure/adapters where practical.

---

79. CLOUD ARCHITECTURE

When Cloudflare is used, appropriate primitives may include:

- Workers
- Durable Objects
- D1
- R2
- KV
- Queues
- Vectorize
- Workflows
- Workers AI

Use each only where its characteristics fit the workload.

Do not introduce Cloudflare services merely because they exist.

For example:

- relational state → D1 where appropriate
- large objects → R2
- strongly coordinated state → Durable Objects
- background jobs → Queues/Workflows
- vector search → Vectorize or another provider
- stateless HTTP → Workers

Cloudflare must remain replaceable.

---

80. MCP

MCP should be treated as an interface/protocol integration.

It is not the entire Raymond architecture.

Raymond should be able to expose capabilities through MCP while also supporting future:

- HTTP APIs
- WebSockets
- mobile protocol
- internal node protocol
- automation interfaces
- other agent interfaces

---

81. SECURITY STANDARDS

Security architecture should be aligned with current authoritative standards and guidance, including where appropriate:

- OWASP
- NIST
- CISA
- OAuth 2.x / PKCE
- MCP security guidance
- Zero Trust principles
- secure software supply chain practices
- AI/agent security practices

When implementing a specific standard, verify its current version and official documentation rather than relying on memory.

---

82. SUPPLY CHAIN SECURITY

Future implementation should consider:

- dependency review
- vulnerability scanning
- lockfiles
- signed/reproducible artifacts where practical
- SBOM
- secret scanning
- static analysis
- container scanning
- code review
- provenance
- release verification

Never put secrets into source control.

---

83. SECRET MANAGEMENT

Secrets must be referenced indirectly.

Concept:

Core
 |
Secret Reference
 |
Secret Provider
 |
Actual Secret

Core should never need to know the actual secret value unless a specific execution boundary legitimately requires it.

---

84. TENANT ISOLATION

Managed instances and future multi-user environments must have strong isolation.

Isolation applies to:

- data
- sessions
- capabilities
- credentials
- policies
- quotas
- execution
- audit
- AI context

---

85. AI SECURITY

AI agents must be treated as potentially untrusted execution planners.

Protect against:

- prompt injection
- tool misuse
- unauthorized data access
- excessive permissions
- secret leakage
- unsafe generated commands
- confused-deputy behavior
- cross-tenant leakage

The policy engine remains authoritative.

---

86. ZERO TRUST MODEL

Do not assume that:

- a node is trusted because it is registered
- an AI is trusted because it is internal
- a provider is trusted because it is popular
- a request is safe because it came from the UI

Continuously verify identity and authorization.

---

87. FAILURE TOLERANCE

Design for:

- provider failure
- node failure
- network failure
- database failure
- deployment failure
- model failure
- credential expiration
- corrupted state
- partial migration
- interrupted synchronization

Every critical subsystem should have explicit failure modes.

---

88. NO SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE

The architecture should progressively remove critical single points of failure.

Examples:

AI Provider A
        ↓
AI Provider B

Node A
  ↓
Node B

Data Replica A
  ↓
Data Replica B

The degree of redundancy should be configurable based on cost and risk.

101. NEW SERVER ONBOARDING

→ INITIALIZE
→ GENERATE IDENTITY
→ REGISTER
→ SECURE CHANNEL
→ HEALTH CHECK
→ CAPABILITY DISCOVERY
→ READY

Eventually Raymond should orchestrate much of this.

118. FINAL ARCHITECTURAL LAWS

These laws must remain true unless the architecture is intentionally revised and the change is explicitly approved.

LAW 1

Core is stable.

LAW 2

Capabilities are replaceable.

LAW 3

Providers are replaceable.

LAW 4

Infrastructure is replaceable.

LAW 5

Data is portable.

LAW 6

AI is not root authority.

LAW 7

Security boundaries are stronger than convenience.

LAW 8

Unknown operations fail closed.

LAW 9

Important actions are auditable.

LAW 10

Critical actions are approval-controlled.

LAW 11

No single provider should own Raymond.

LAW 12

No single node should be able to destroy the entire system.

LAW 13

New capabilities should not require Core rewrites unless absolutely necessary.

LAW 14

Every major component must define contracts.

LAW 15

Every major change must be testable and reversible.

LAW 16

Performance must be designed from the beginning.

LAW 17

Offline/degraded operation is a first-class architectural concern.

LAW 18

Secrets never belong in normal application state.

LAW 19

Data access is permissioned and audited.

LAW 20

Self-evolution is controlled evolution, not unrestricted self-modification.

LAW 21

The user remains the authority for sensitive decisions.

LAW 22

Architecture must support one node today and many nodes tomorrow.

LAW 23

Raymond must be portable across infrastructure providers.

LAW 24

Mobile is a secure control surface, not the permanent home of Raymond data.

LAW 25

A failure of GitHub, Cloudflare, a VPS, an AI provider, a data node or a phone must not automatically mean the death of Raymond.

---

119. THE FINAL GOAL

The final Raymond should allow its owner to think in terms of:

"What do I want Raymond to accomplish?"

rather than:

"Which API do I need?"
"Which server should I log into?"
"Which application should I install?"
"Which provider should I configure manually?"

The owner should eventually be able to say:

«"Add this server."»

«"Connect this account."»

«"Move this service."»

«"Use local AI."»

«"Back up this data."»

«"Search my knowledge base."»

«"Connect this device."»

«"Add this capability."»

«"Move Raymond to this infrastructure."»

«"Recover the failed node."»

«"Show me what is unhealthy."»

Raymond should transform these intentions into controlled, observable, secure Operations.

فایل ۶: schema.sql
این ساختار دیتابیس اولیه‌ست. شامل جداول پایه‌ای که همون معماری event-based و capability-based رو پشتیبانی می‌کنه.

sql
-- ============================================
-- RAYMOND v0.1 — Base Schema
-- ============================================

-- Conversations (chat threads)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversations (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'New chat',
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000)
);

-- Messages (individual chat messages)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  conversation_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('user', 'assistant', 'system')),
  content TEXT NOT NULL,
  provider TEXT,
  model TEXT,
  tokens_in INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  tokens_out INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  latency_ms INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000),
  FOREIGN KEY (conversation_id) REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_conversation 
  ON messages(conversation_id, created_at);

-- Capability Registry (plugin system)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS capabilities (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.1.0',
  enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  config TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  manifest TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000),
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000)
);

-- Operations (every meaningful action becomes an Operation)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS operations (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  capability_id TEXT,
  operation_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  actor TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'owner',
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' 
    CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','running','completed','failed','rejected','rolled_back')),
  input TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  output TEXT,
  error TEXT,
  risk TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'low' CHECK (risk IN ('low','medium','high','critical')),
  requires_approval INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  approved_by TEXT,
  approved_at INTEGER,
  started_at INTEGER,
  finished_at INTEGER,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000),
  FOREIGN KEY (capability_id) REFERENCES capabilities(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_operations_status ON operations(status, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_operations_capability ON operations(capability_id, created_at DESC);

-- Event Bus (communication between modules)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  topic TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  source TEXT,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' 
    CHECK (status IN ('pending','processing','delivered','failed')),
  attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  error TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000),
  processed_at INTEGER
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_topic ON events(topic, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_status ON events(status, created_at);

-- Audit Log (immutable record of important actions)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  actor TEXT NOT NULL,
  action TEXT NOT NULL,
  resource_type TEXT,
  resource_id TEXT,
  metadata TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  ip TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_created ON audit_log(created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_actor ON audit_log(actor, created_at DESC);

-- Settings (key-value store for app config)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS settings (
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch() * 1000)
);

-- Seed default settings
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO settings (key, value) VALUES 
  ('ai.default_provider', '"workers-ai"'),
  ('ai.default_model', '"@cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct"'),
  ('system.version', '"0.1.0"');

فایل ۸: README.md
markdown
# Raymond

A modular, provider-independent personal AI control plane.

## Architecture

- **Core** (`src/worker/core/`) — stable, rarely changes
- **Capabilities** (`src/worker/capabilities/`) — pluggable modules
- **Adapters** (`src/worker/adapters/`) — provider-specific implementations
- **UI** (`src/ui/`) — thin client, no business logic

Modules communicate through an **Event Bus** — no direct dependencies.

## Stack

- Cloudflare Workers (runtime)
- Hono (HTTP framework)
- Cloudflare D1 (database)
- Workers AI (free AI models)
- React + Vite (UI)

## Local Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
Deploy
bash
npm run deploy
Status
v0.1 — Base chat + AI routing

Future: Telegram, X, Email, VPN module, Data platform, Local AI

# Raymond

A modular, provider-independent personal AI control plane.

## Architecture

- **Core** (`src/worker/core/`) — stable, rarely changes
- **Capabilities** (`src/worker/capabilities/`) — pluggable modules
- **Adapters** (`src/worker/adapters/`) — provider-specific implementations
- **UI** (`src/ui/`) — thin client, no business logic

Modules communicate through an **Event Bus** — no direct dependencies.

## Stack

- Cloudflare Workers (runtime)
- Hono (HTTP framework)
- Cloudflare D1 (database)
- Workers AI (free AI models)
- React + Vite (UI)

## Local Development

    npm install
    npm run dev

## Deploy

    npm run deploy

## Status

- v0.1 — Base chat + AI routing
- Future: Telegram, X, Email, VPN module, Data platform, Local AI

@'
// Cryptographically random IDs

export function newId(prefix = ""): string {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(16);
  crypto.getRandomValues(bytes);
  const hex = Array.from(bytes)
    .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("");
  return prefix ? `${prefix}_${hex}` : hex;
}

export function now(): number {
  return Date.now();
}

// D1 database helper

export interface Env {
  DB: D1Database;
  AI: Ai;
  ASSETS: Fetcher;
  ENVIRONMENT: string;
  APP_NAME: string;
}

export async function queryFirst<T = unknown>(
  db: D1Database,
  sql: string,
  ...params: unknown[]
): Promise<T | null> {
  const stmt = db.prepare(sql).bind(...params);
  return (await stmt.first<T>()) ?? null;
}

export async function queryAll<T = unknown>(
  db: D1Database,
  sql: string,
  ...params: unknown[]
): Promise<T[]> {
  const stmt = db.prepare(sql).bind(...params);
  const result = await stmt.all<T>();
  return result.results ?? [];
}

export async function run(
  db: D1Database,
  sql: string,
  ...params: unknown[]
): Promise<D1Result> {
  const stmt = db.prepare(sql).bind(...params);
  return await stmt.run();
}

# ---- src/worker/core/event-bus.ts ----
@'
// Event Bus — modules talk through events, never directly.
//
// Usage:
//   await bus.publish(env, "message.received", { text: "hi" }, "telegram");
//   await bus.subscribe(env, "message.received", async (payload) => {...});

import { newId, now } from "./id";
import { queryAll, run } from "./db";
import type { Env, RaymondEvent } from "./db";

export type EventHandler = (payload: unknown, event: RaymondEvent) => Promise<void>;

const handlers = new Map<string, EventHandler[]>();

export const bus = {
  register(topic: string, handler: EventHandler): void {
    const list = handlers.get(topic) ?? [];
    list.push(handler);
    handlers.set(topic, list);
  },

  async publish(
    env: Env,
    topic: string,
    payload: unknown,
    source = "core"
  ): Promise<string> {
    const id = newId("evt");
    await run(
      env.DB,
      `INSERT INTO events (id, topic, payload, source, status, attempts, created_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'pending', 0, ?)`,
      id,
      topic,
      JSON.stringify(payload),
      source,
      now()
    );

    // Deliver in-process immediately (fire and forget)
    void this.deliver(env, id);

    return id;
  },

  async deliver(env: Env, eventId: string): Promise<void> {
    const evt = await queryAll<RaymondEvent>(
      env.DB,
      `SELECT * FROM events WHERE id = ? LIMIT 1`,
      eventId
    );
    if (!evt.length) return;
    const event = evt[0];

    await run(
      env.DB,
      `UPDATE events SET status = 'processing', attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = ?`,
      event.id
    );

    const list = handlers.get(event.topic) ?? [];
    let ok = true;
    let lastError: string | undefined;

    for (const handler of list) {
      try {
        await handler(JSON.parse(event.payload), event);
      } catch (err) {
        ok = false;
        lastError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      }
    }

    await run(
      env.DB,
      `UPDATE events 
       SET status = ?, error = ?, processed_at = ? 
       WHERE id = ?`,
      ok ? "delivered" : "failed",
      lastError ?? null,
      now(),
      event.id
    );
  },

  async retryFailed(env: Env, limit = 50): Promise<number> {
    const failed = await queryAll<RaymondEvent>(
      env.DB,
      `SELECT id FROM events 
       WHERE status = 'failed' AND attempts < 5 
       ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT ?`,
      limit
    );
    for (const row of failed) {
      await this.deliver(env, row.id);
    }
    return failed.length;
  },
};
'@ | Set-Content -Path "src\worker\core\event-bus.ts" -Encoding UTF8

@'
// Capability Registry — every feature is a capability.
//
// A capability has:
//   - id, name, version
//   - manifest (metadata)
//   - enabled flag
//   - config (JSON)
//
// Capabilities NEVER touch the Core directly. They subscribe to events,
// register operations, and are exposed via the API.

import { newId, now } from "./id";
import { queryAll, run } from "./db";
import type { Env } from "./db";
import type { Capability } from "../../shared/types";

export interface CapabilityManifest {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  version: string;
  description?: string;
  author?: string;
  permissions?: string[];
  events_subscribed?: string[];
  events_published?: string[];
}

const registeredManifests = new Map<string, CapabilityManifest>();

export const registry = {
  register(manifest: CapabilityManifest): void {
    registeredManifests.set(manifest.id, manifest);
  },

  get(id: string): CapabilityManifest | undefined {
    return registeredManifests.get(id);
  },

  list(): CapabilityManifest[] {
    return Array.from(registeredManifests.values());
  },

  async syncToDb(env: Env): Promise<void> {
    for (const m of registeredManifests.values()) {
      const existing = await queryAll<Capability>(
        env.DB,
        `SELECT id FROM capabilities WHERE id = ? LIMIT 1`,
        m.id
      );
      if (existing.length) {
        await run(
          env.DB,
          `UPDATE capabilities 
           SET name = ?, version = ?, manifest = ?, updated_at = ?
           WHERE id = ?`,
          m.name,
          m.version,
          JSON.stringify(m),
          now(),
          m.id
        );
      } else {
        await run(
          env.DB,
          `INSERT INTO capabilities (id, name, version, enabled, config, manifest, created_at, updated_at)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, 1, '{}', ?, ?, ?)`,
          m.id,
          m.name,
          m.version,
          JSON.stringify(m),
          now(),
          now()
        );
      }
    }
  },
};

@'
// Operation model — every meaningful action becomes an Operation.
//
// Operation lifecycle:
//   pending -> approved -> running -> completed
//                                   -> failed
//                                   -> rolled_back
//   pending -> rejected

import { newId, now } from "./id";
import { queryAll, run } from "./db";
import type { Env } from "./db";
import type { Operation, OperationStatus, RiskLevel } from "../../shared/types";

export interface CreateOperationInput {
  capability_id?: string;
  operation_type: string;
  actor?: string;
  input?: unknown;
  risk?: RiskLevel;
  requires_approval?: boolean;
}

export const operations = {
  async create(env: Env, input: CreateOperationInput): Promise<Operation> {
    const op: Operation = {
      id: newId("op"),
      capability_id: input.capability_id,
      operation_type: input.operation_type,
      actor: input.actor ?? "owner",
      status: "pending",
      input: JSON.stringify(input.input ?? {}),
      risk: input.risk ?? "low",
      requires_approval: input.requires_approval ? 1 : 0,
      created_at: now(),
    };

    await run(
      env.DB,
      `INSERT INTO operations 
        (id, capability_id, operation_type, actor, status, input, risk, requires_approval, created_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      op.id,
      op.capability_id ?? null,
      op.operation_type,
      op.actor,
      op.status,
      op.input,
      op.risk,
      op.requires_approval,
      op.created_at
    );

    return op;
  },

  async updateStatus(
    env: Env,
    id: string,
    status: OperationStatus,
    patch: Partial<Pick<Operation, "output" | "error" | "approved_by" | "approved_at" | "started_at" | "finished_at">> = {}
  ): Promise<void> {
    const fields: string[] = ["status = ?"];
    const params: unknown[] = [status];

    if (patch.output !== undefined) { fields.push("output = ?"); params.push(patch.output); }
    if (patch.error !== undefined) { fields.push("error = ?"); params.push(patch.error); }
    if (patch.approved_by !== undefined) { fields.push("approved_by = ?"); params.push(patch.approved_by); }
    if (patch.approved_at !== undefined) { fields.push("approved_at = ?"); params.push(patch.approved_at); }
    if (patch.started_at !== undefined) { fields.push("started_at = ?"); params.push(patch.started_at); }
    if (patch.finished_at !== undefined) { fields.push("finished_at = ?"); params.push(patch.finished_at); }

    params.push(id);
    await run(env.DB, `UPDATE operations SET ${fields.join(", ")} WHERE id = ?`, ...params);
  },

  async get(env: Env, id: string): Promise<Operation | null> {
    const rows = await queryAll<Operation>(
      env.DB,
      `SELECT * FROM operations WHERE id = ? LIMIT 1`,
      id
    );
    return rows[0] ?? null;
  },

  async list(env: Env, limit = 100): Promise<Operation[]> {
    return await queryAll<Operation>(
      env.DB,
      `SELECT * FROM operations ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?`,
      limit
    );
  },
};

@'
// AI Chat capability — base capability for v0.1.
//
// Subscribes to: chat.message.sent
// Publishes:     chat.message.received

import { newId, now } from "../core/id";
import { bus } from "../core/event-bus";
import { audit } from "../core/audit";
import { queryAll, run } from "../core/db";
import type { Env } from "../core/db";
import type { Message } from "../../shared/types";
import { aiRouter } from "../adapters/ai-router";

export interface ChatMessagePayload {
  conversation_id: string;
  content: string;
  provider?: string;
  model?: string;
}

export const aiChatCapability = {
  manifest: {
    id: "ai-chat",
    name: "AI Chat",
    version: "0.1.0",
    description: "Chat with AI through the Router",
    events_subscribed: ["chat.message.sent"],
    events_published: ["chat.message.received"],
  },

  register(): void {
    bus.register("chat.message.sent", async (payload) => {
      const p = payload as ChatMessagePayload;
      await this.handle(p);
    });
  },

  async handle(payload: ChatMessagePayload): Promise<void> {
    // NOTE: handler is invoked in the event bus context;
    // env is retrieved via the AI router call chain. For v0.1 we store
    // the env globally at startup in the worker entry.
    const env = getEnv();
    if (!env) return;

    const { conversation_id, content, provider, model } = payload;

    // 1. Store user message
    const userMsgId = newId("msg");
    await run(
      env.DB,
      `INSERT INTO messages (id, conversation_id, role, content, created_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, 'user', ?, ?)`,
      userMsgId,
      conversation_id,
      content,
      now()
    );

    // 2. Load history (last 20 messages)
    const history = await queryAll<Message>(
      env.DB,
      `SELECT role, content FROM messages 
       WHERE conversation_id = ? 
       ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 40`,
      conversation_id
    );

    // 3. Route to AI
    const started = now();
    const result = await aiRouter.complete(env, {
      messages: history.map((m) => ({ role: m.role, content: m.content })),
      provider,
      model,
    });
    const latency = now() - started;

    // 4. Store assistant reply
    const assistantId = newId("msg");
    await run(
      env.DB,
      `INSERT INTO messages 
        (id, conversation_id, role, content, provider, model, latency_ms, created_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, 'assistant', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      assistantId,
      conversation_id,
      result.content,
      result.provider,
      result.model,
      latency,
      now()
    );

    // 5. Bump conversation updated_at
    await run(
      env.DB,
      `UPDATE conversations SET updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?`,
      now(),
      conversation_id
    );

    // 6. Audit
    await audit(env, {
      actor: "owner",
      action: "chat.message",
      resource_type: "conversation",
      resource_id: conversation_id,
      metadata: { provider: result.provider, model: result.model, latency_ms: latency },
    });

    // 7. Publish event
    await bus.publish(
      env,
      "chat.message.received",
      { conversation_id, message_id: assistantId },
      "ai-chat"
    );
  },
};

// Simple env holder set by the worker entry at startup.
let _env: Env | null = null;
export function setEnv(env: Env): void { _env = env; }
export function getEnv(): Env | null { return _env; }
'@ | Set-Content -Path "src\worker\capabilities\ai-chat.ts" -Encoding UTF8

# ---- src/worker/adapters/ai-router.ts ----
@'
// AI Router — chooses the best provider/model for the task.
//
// v0.1 supports:
//   - workers-ai  (Cloudflare Workers AI, free tier)
//
// Future adapters can be added in this file or as siblings.
// The router is provider-agnostic: callers just ask for a completion.

import type { Env } from "../core/db";

export interface ChatMessage {
  role: "user" | "assistant" | "system";
  content: string;
}

export interface CompleteInput {
  messages: ChatMessage[];
  provider?: string;
  model?: string;
  temperature?: number;
}

export interface CompleteOutput {
  content: string;
  provider: string;
  model: string;
}

const DEFAULT_PROVIDER = "workers-ai";
const DEFAULT_MODEL = "@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct";

export const aiRouter = {
  async complete(env: Env, input: CompleteInput): Promise<CompleteOutput> {
    const provider = input.provider ?? DEFAULT_PROVIDER;
    const model = input.model ?? DEFAULT_MODEL;

    switch (provider) {
      case "workers-ai":
        return await completeWorkersAI(env, model, input);
      default:
        throw new Error(`Unknown provider: ${provider}`);
    }
  },
};

async function completeWorkersAI(
  env: Env,
  model: string,
  input: CompleteInput
): Promise<CompleteOutput> {
  const response = (await env.AI.run(model as never, {
    messages: input.messages,
    temperature: input.temperature ?? 0.7,
  })) as { response?: string };

  const content = response?.response ?? "";
  if (!content) throw new Error("Empty response from Workers AI");

  return { content, provider: "workers-ai", model };
}
'@ | Set-Content -Path "src\worker\adapters\ai-router.ts" -Encoding UTF8

// Chat routes

import { Hono } from "hono";
import { newId, now } from "../core/id";
import { bus } from "../core/event-bus";
import { queryAll, run } from "../core/db";
import type { Env } from "../core/db";
import type { Conversation, Message } from "../../shared/types";

export const chatRoutes = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>();

// Create a new conversation
chatRoutes.post("/conversations", async (c) => {
  const id = newId("conv");
  const title = "New chat";
  await run(
    c.env.DB,
    `INSERT INTO conversations (id, title, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
    id,
    title,
    now(),
    now()
  );
  return c.json({ id, title, created_at: now(), updated_at: now() });
});

// List conversations
chatRoutes.get("/conversations", async (c) => {
  const rows = await queryAll<Conversation>(
    c.env.DB,
    `SELECT * FROM conversations ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 100`
  );
  return c.json(rows);
});

// Get messages of a conversation
chatRoutes.get("/conversations/:id/messages", async (c) => {
  const id = c.req.param("id");
  const rows = await queryAll<Message>(
    c.env.DB,
    `SELECT * FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC`,
    id
  );
  return c.json(rows);
});

// Send a message
chatRoutes.post("/conversations/:id/messages", async (c) => {
  const conversationId = c.req.param("id");
  const body = await c.req.json<{ content: string; provider?: string; model?: string }>();

  if (!body?.content?.trim()) {
    return c.json({ error: "content is required" }, 400);
  }

  await bus.publish(
    c.env,
    "chat.message.sent",
    {
      conversation_id: conversationId,
      content: body.content,
      provider: body.provider,
      model: body.model,
    },
    "api"
  );

  return c.json({ ok: true });
});

// Delete a conversation
chatRoutes.delete("/conversations/:id", async (c) => {
  const id = c.req.param("id");
  await run(c.env.DB, `DELETE FROM conversations WHERE id = ?`, id);
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});

# ---- src/worker/index.ts ----
@'
// Raymond Worker entry point.
//
// Wires together: Hono, capabilities, event bus, registry, routes.

import { Hono } from "hono";
import { cors } from "hono/cors";
import type { Env } from "./core/db";
import { registry } from "./core/registry";
import { bus } from "./core/event-bus";
import { aiChatCapability, setEnv } from "./capabilities/ai-chat";
import { chatRoutes } from "./routes/chat";
import { systemRoutes } from "./routes/system";

type Bindings = Env;

const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }>();

// Middleware
app.use("*", cors());

// Attach env globally (used by capabilities)
app.use("*", async (c, next) => {
  setEnv(c.env);
  await next();
});

// Routes
app.route("/api/chat", chatRoutes);
app.route("/api/system", systemRoutes);

// Root API info
app.get("/api", (c) => {
  return c.json({
    app: c.env.APP_NAME ?? "Raymond",
    version: "0.1.0",
    endpoints: [
      "GET  /api/system/health",
      "GET  /api/system/capabilities",
      "GET  /api/system/operations",
      "GET  /api/chat/conversations",
      "POST /api/chat/conversations",
      "GET  /api/chat/conversations/:id/messages",
      "POST /api/chat/conversations/:id/messages",
      "DEL  /api/chat/conversations/:id",
    ],
  });
});

// 404 for unknown API routes
app.all("/api/*", (c) => c.json({ error: "Not found" }, 404));

// Register capabilities + sync registry (idempotent, safe to call each request)
let bootstrapped = false;
async function bootstrap(env: Env): Promise<void> {
  if (bootstrapped) return;
  bootstrapped = true;

  // Register capabilities
  registry.register(aiChatCapability.manifest);
  aiChatCapability.register();

  // Sync to DB
  try {
    await registry.syncToDb(env);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("Registry sync failed:", err);
  }
}

// Static assets handler (SPA)
app.all("*", async (c) => {
  await bootstrap(c.env);
  return c.env.ASSETS.fetch(c.req.raw);
});

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env, ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<Response> {
    await bootstrap(env);
    return app.fetch(request, env, ctx);
  },
} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

# ---- src/worker/adapters/openrouter.ts ----
@'
// OpenRouter adapter — access to many free models through one API.
//
// Setup: get a free key at https://openrouter.ai/keys
// Then run:  wrangler secret put OPENROUTER_API_KEY
//
// Free models include (as of writing):
//   - deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324:free
//   - meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free
//   - google/gemma-3-27b-it:free
//   - qwen/qwen-2.5-72b-instruct:free
//   - mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct:free

import type { Env } from "../core/db";

export interface ChatMessage {
  role: "user" | "assistant" | "system";
  content: string;
}

export interface OpenRouterInput {
  model: string;
  messages: ChatMessage[];
  temperature?: number;
  apiKey: string;
}

export interface OpenRouterOutput {
  content: string;
  model: string;
}

const OPENROUTER_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions";

export async function callOpenRouter(
  input: OpenRouterInput
): Promise<OpenRouterOutput> {
  const res = await fetch(OPENROUTER_URL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Authorization": `Bearer ${input.apiKey}`,
      "HTTP-Referer": "https://raymond.workers.dev",
      "X-Title": "Raymond",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: input.model,
      messages: input.messages,
      temperature: input.temperature ?? 0.7,
    }),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`OpenRouter error ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 300)}`);
  }

  const json = (await res.json()) as {
    choices?: Array<{ message?: { content?: string } }>;
    model?: string;
  };

  const content = json.choices?.[0]?.message?.content ?? "";
  if (!content) throw new Error("Empty response from OpenRouter");

  return { content, model: json.model ?? input.model };
}

export function getOpenRouterKey(env: Env): string | null {
  const key = (env as unknown as { OPENROUTER_API_KEY?: string }).OPENROUTER_API_KEY;
  return key && key.length > 0 ? key : null;
}
'@ | Set-Content -Path "src\worker\adapters\openrouter.ts" -Encoding UTF8

@'
// Ollama adapter — talk to a local Ollama server (for later, on your VPS).
//
// Setup (later): run Ollama somewhere, expose it via HTTPS, then:
//   wrangler secret put OLLAMA_URL     (e.g. https://ollama.yourdomain.com)
//   wrangler secret put OLLAMA_API_KEY (if you put a proxy in front)

import type { Env } from "../core/db";

export interface ChatMessage {
  role: "user" | "assistant" | "system";
  content: string;
}

export interface OllamaInput {
  url: string;
  model: string;
  messages: ChatMessage[];
  temperature?: number;
}

export interface OllamaOutput {
  content: string;
  model: string;
}

export async function callOllama(input: OllamaInput): Promise<OllamaOutput> {
  const res = await fetch(`${input.url.replace(/\/$/, "")}/api/chat`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: input.model,
      messages: input.messages,
      stream: false,
      options: { temperature: input.temperature ?? 0.7 },
    }),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Ollama error ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 300)}`);
  }

  const json = (await res.json()) as {
    message?: { content?: string };
    model?: string;
  };

  const content = json.message?.content ?? "";
  if (!content) throw new Error("Empty response from Ollama");

  return { content, model: json.model ?? input.model };
}

export function getOllamaUrl(env: Env): string | null {
  const url = (env as unknown as { OLLAMA_URL?: string }).OLLAMA_URL;
  return url && url.length > 0 ? url : null;
}

# ---- src/worker/adapters/ai-router.ts (updated) ----
@'
// AI Router — chooses the best provider/model for the task.
//
// Supported providers:
//   - workers-ai   (Cloudflare Workers AI, free tier, default)
//   - openrouter   (many free models via OpenRouter, needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
//   - ollama       (local, needs OLLAMA_URL) — for later on VPS
//
// Fallback chain: if the requested provider fails, try the next available one.

import type { Env } from "../core/db";
import { callOpenRouter, getOpenRouterKey } from "./openrouter";
import { callOllama, getOllamaUrl } from "./ollama";

export interface ChatMessage {
  role: "user" | "assistant" | "system";
  content: string;
}

export interface CompleteInput {
  messages: ChatMessage[];
  provider?: string;
  model?: string;
  temperature?: number;
}

export interface CompleteOutput {
  content: string;
  provider: string;
  model: string;
}

export const DEFAULT_PROVIDER = "workers-ai";
export const DEFAULT_WORKERS_AI_MODEL = "@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct";
export const DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_MODEL = "deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324:free";

export interface ProviderInfo {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  available: boolean;
  default_model: string;
  description: string;
}

export function listProviders(env: Env): ProviderInfo[] {
  return [
    {
      id: "workers-ai",
      name: "Cloudflare Workers AI",
      available: true,
      default_model: DEFAULT_WORKERS_AI_MODEL,
      description: "Free tier, built into Cloudflare, no API key needed",
    },
    {
      id: "openrouter",
      name: "OpenRouter",
      available: !!getOpenRouterKey(env),
      default_model: DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_MODEL,
      description: "Access to many free models; requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY",
    },
    {
      id: "ollama",
      name: "Ollama (local)",
      available: !!getOllamaUrl(env),
      default_model: "qwen2.5:7b",
      description: "Local models on your own server; requires OLLAMA_URL",
    },
  ];
}

export const aiRouter = {
  async complete(env: Env, input: CompleteInput): Promise<CompleteOutput> {
    const provider = input.provider ?? DEFAULT_PROVIDER;

    // Try the requested provider first
    try {
      return await this.callProvider(env, provider, input);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(`Provider "${provider}" failed:`, err);

      // Fallback chain
      const fallbacks = ["workers-ai", "openrouter"].filter((p) => p !== provider);
      for (const fb of fallbacks) {
        try {
          const info = listProviders(env).find((p) => p.id === fb);
          if (!info?.available) continue;
          return await this.callProvider(env, fb, { ...input, model: undefined });
        } catch (e2) {
          console.error(`Fallback "${fb}" failed:`, e2);
        }
      }
      throw err;
    }
  },

  async callProvider(
    env: Env,
    provider: string,
    input: CompleteInput
  ): Promise<CompleteOutput> {
    switch (provider) {
      case "workers-ai": {
        const model = input.model ?? DEFAULT_WORKERS_AI_MODEL;
        const response = (await env.AI.run(model as never, {
          messages: input.messages,
          temperature: input.temperature ?? 0.7,
        })) as { response?: string };
        const content = response?.response ?? "";
        if (!content) throw new Error("Empty response from Workers AI");
        return { content, provider: "workers-ai", model };
      }

      case "openrouter": {
        const key = getOpenRouterKey(env);
        if (!key) throw new Error("OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set");
        const model = input.model ?? DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_MODEL;
        const out = await callOpenRouter({
          model,
          messages: input.messages,
          temperature: input.temperature,
          apiKey: key,
        });
        return { content: out.content, provider: "openrouter", model: out.model };
      }

      case "ollama": {
        const url = getOllamaUrl(env);
        if (!url) throw new Error("OLLAMA_URL is not set");
        const model = input.model ?? "qwen2.5:7b";
        const out = await callOllama({
          url,
          model,
          messages: input.messages,
          temperature: input.temperature,
        });
        return { content: out.content, provider: "ollama", model: out.model };
      }

      default:
        throw new Error(`Unknown provider: ${provider}`);
    }
  },
};

# ---- src/ui/lib/api.ts ----
@'
// API client for Raymond backend

import type { Conversation, Message } from "../../shared/types";

const BASE = "/api";

async function req<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}${path}`, {
    ...init,
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...(init?.headers ?? {}),
    },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text().catch(() => "");
    throw new Error(`${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  return (await res.json()) as T;
}

export interface ProviderInfo {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  available: boolean;
  default_model: string;
  description: string;
}

export const api = {
  health: () => req<{ ok: boolean; app: string; env: string; time: number }>("/system/health"),

  listProviders: () => req<ProviderInfo[]>("/system/providers"),

  listConversations: () => req<Conversation[]>("/chat/conversations"),

  createConversation: () =>
    req<Conversation>("/chat/conversations", { method: "POST" }),

  getMessages: (id: string) =>
    req<Message[]>(`/chat/conversations/${id}/messages`),

  sendMessage: (id: string, content: string, provider?: string, model?: string) =>
    req<{ ok: boolean }>(`/chat/conversations/${id}/messages`, {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({ content, provider, model }),
    }),

  deleteConversation: (id: string) =>
    req<{ ok: boolean }>(`/chat/conversations/${id}`, { method: "DELETE" }),
};
'@ | Set-Content -Path "src\ui\lib\api.ts" -Encoding UTF8

# ---- src/ui/components/Composer.tsx ----
@'
import { useRef, useState, useEffect } from "react";

interface Props {
  onSend: (text: string) => void;
  disabled: boolean;
}

export function Composer({ onSend, disabled }: Props) {
  const [text, setText] = useState("");
  const ref = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current;
    if (!el) return;
    el.style.height = "auto";
    el.style.height = Math.min(el.scrollHeight, 200) + "px";
  }, [text]);

  const submit = () => {
    const t = text.trim();
    if (!t || disabled) return;
    onSend(t);
    setText("");
  };

  return (
    <div className="composer">
      <div className="composer-inner">
        <textarea
          ref={ref}
          rows={1}
          placeholder="Ask Raymond anything..."
          value={text}
          onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === "Enter" && !e.shiftKey) {
              e.preventDefault();
              submit();
            }
          }}
          disabled={disabled}
        />
        <button onClick={submit} disabled={disabled || !text.trim()} title="Send">
          {disabled ? "…" : "↑"}
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export function MessageList({ messages, loading }: Props) {

  if (messages.length === 0 && !loading) {

        <div className="welcome">

          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className="messages">
      {messages.map((m) => (
        <div key={m.id} className={`msg ${m.role}`}>
          <div className="msg-avatar">{m.role === "user" ? "U" : "R"}</div>
          <div className="msg-body">
            <div className="msg-role">{m.role === "user" ? "You" : "Raymond"}</div>
            <div className="msg-content">{m.content}</div>
            {m.role === "assistant" && (m.provider || m.latency_ms) && (
              <div className="msg-meta">
                {m.provider && <span>{m.provider}</span>}
                {m.model && <span> · {m.model}</span>}
                {m.latency_ms ? <span> · {m.latency_ms}ms</span> : null}
              </div>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}

      {loading && (
        <div className="msg assistant">
          <div className="msg-avatar">R</div>
          <div className="msg-body">
            <div className="msg-role">Raymond</div>
            <div className="typing">
              <span /><span /><span />
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

      <div ref={endRef} />

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { api, type ProviderInfo } from "../lib/api";

interface Props {
  onBack: () => void;
}

interface Health {
  ok: boolean;
  app: string;
  env: string;
  time: number;
}

export function Dashboard({ onBack }: Props) {
  const [providers, setProviders] = useState<ProviderInfo[]>([]);
  const [health, setHealth] = useState<Health | null>(null);
  const [caps, setCaps] = useState<unknown>(null);
  const [ops, setOps] = useState<unknown[]>([]);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    (async () => {
      try {
        const [h, p, c, o] = await Promise.all([
          api.health(),

        setHealth(h);

        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
      }
    })();
  }, []);

  return (
    <div className="dashboard">
      <button
        onClick={onBack}

              <div className="provider-name">{p.name}</div>
              <div className="provider-desc">{p.description}</div>
            </div>
            <span className={`badge ${p.available ? "ok" : "off"}`}>
              {p.available ? "Ready" : "Not configured"}
            </span>

        ))}
      </div>

      <div className="card">
        <h3>Capabilities</h3>

          <div className="kv">

# ---- src/ui/App.tsx ----
@'
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, useCallback } from "react";
import { api, type ProviderInfo } from "./lib/api";
import { Sidebar } from "./components/Sidebar";
import { MessageList } from "./components/MessageList";
import { Composer } from "./components/Composer";
import { Dashboard } from "./components/Dashboard";
import type { Conversation, Message } from "../shared/types";

type View = "chat" | "dashboard";

export default function App() {
  const [conversations, setConversations] = useState<Conversation[]>([]);
  const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState<Message[]>([]);
  const [providers, setProviders] = useState<ProviderInfo[]>([]);
  const [selectedProvider, setSelectedProvider] = useState<string>("workers-ai");
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [healthy, setHealthy] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
  const [view, setView] = useState<View>("chat");
  const [sidebarOpen, setSidebarOpen] = useState(false);

  const pollRef = useRef<number | null>(null);

  // Initial load
  useEffect(() => {
    (async () => {
      try {
        await api.health();
        setHealthy(true);
      } catch {
        setHealthy(false);
      }
      try {
        const [convs, provs] = await Promise.all([
          api.listConversations(),
          api.listProviders(),
        ]);
        setConversations(convs);
        setProviders(provs);
        const firstAvailable = provs.find((p) => p.available);
        if (firstAvailable) setSelectedProvider(firstAvailable.id);
      } catch (e) {
        console.error(e);
      }
    })();
  }, []);

  // Load messages when active changes
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!activeId) { setMessages([]); return; }
    (async () => {
      try {
        const msgs = await api.getMessages(activeId);
        setMessages(msgs);
      } catch (e) {
        console.error(e);
      }
    })();
  }, [activeId]);

  // Poll for new messages while loading
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!loading || !activeId) return;
    pollRef.current = window.setInterval(async () => {
      try {
        const msgs = await api.getMessages(activeId);
        setMessages(msgs);
        const last = msgs[msgs.length - 1];
        if (last?.role === "assistant") {
          setLoading(false);
          if (pollRef.current) window.clearInterval(pollRef.current);
        }
      } catch (e) {
        console.error(e);
      }
    }, 1200);
    return () => {
      if (pollRef.current) window.clearInterval(pollRef.current);
    };
  }, [loading, activeId]);

  const newConversation = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      const conv = await api.createConversation();
      setConversations((prev) => [conv, ...prev]);
      setActiveId(conv.id);
      setMessages([]);
      setView("chat");
      setSidebarOpen(false);
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(e);
    }
  }, []);

  const deleteConversation = useCallback(async (id: string) => {
    try {
      await api.deleteConversation(id);
      setConversations((prev) => prev.filter((c) => c.id !== id));
      if (activeId === id) {
        setActiveId(null);
        setMessages([]);
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(e);
    }
  }, [activeId]);

  const send = useCallback(async (text: string) => {
    let convId = activeId;
    if (!convId) {
      const conv = await api.createConversation();
      setConversations((prev) => [conv, ...prev]);
      setActiveId(conv.id);
      convId = conv.id;
    }

    // Optimistic user message
    const temp: Message = {
      id: "temp_" + Date.now(),
      conversation_id: convId,
      role: "user",
      content: text,
      created_at: Date.now(),
    };
    setMessages((prev) => [...prev, temp]);
    setLoading(true);

    try {
      const info = providers.find((p) => p.id === selectedProvider);
      await api.sendMessage(convId, text, selectedProvider, info?.default_model);
      // Refresh conversation title in sidebar (first user message becomes title)
      setConversations((prev) =>
        prev.map((c) =>
          c.id === convId && c.title === "New chat"
            ? { ...c, title: text.slice(0, 40) }
            : c
        )
      );
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(e);
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [activeId, providers, selectedProvider]);

  const activeConv = conversations.find((c) => c.id === activeId);

  return (
    <div className="app">
      <Sidebar
        conversations={conversations}
        activeId={activeId}
        open={sidebarOpen}
        onClose={() => setSidebarOpen(false)}
        onSelect={(id) => { setActiveId(id); setView("chat"); setSidebarOpen(false); }}
        onNew={newConversation}
        onDelete={deleteConversation}
        onOpenDashboard={() => { setView("dashboard"); setSidebarOpen(false); }}
        healthy={healthy}
      />

      <main className="chat">
        {view === "dashboard" ? (
          <Dashboard onBack={() => setView("chat")} />
        ) : (
          <>
            <header className="chat-header">
              <button
                className="menu-btn"
                onClick={() => setSidebarOpen(true)}
                title="Menu"
              >
                ☰
              </button>
              <div className="chat-title">
                {activeConv?.title ?? "New chat"}
              </div>
              <div className="provider-picker">
                <select
                  value={selectedProvider}
                  onChange={(e) => setSelectedProvider(e.target.value)}
                >
                  {providers.map((p) => (
                    <option key={p.id} value={p.id} disabled={!p.available}>
                      {p.name}{p.available ? "" : " (off)"}
                    </option>
                  ))}
                </select>
              </div>
            </header>

            <MessageList messages={messages} loading={loading} />

            <Composer onSend={send} disabled={loading} />
          </>
        )}
      </main>
    </div>
  );
}
'@ | Set-Content -Path "src\ui\App.tsx" -Encoding UTF8

# -- Create D1 database
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "[4/7] Creating D1 database 'raymond-db'..." -ForegroundColor Yellow

$dbId = $null

# Check if DB already exists by listing
$listOutput = npx wrangler d1 list 2>&1 | Out-String

if ($listOutput -match "raymond-db") {
    Write-Host "       Database already exists, reading its ID..." -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    # Extract the ID from the list output (line containing raymond-db)
    $lines = $listOutput -split "`n"
    foreach ($line in $lines) {
        if ($line -match "raymond-db") {
            # Usually UUIDs are in the line, grab first UUID-like string
            if ($line -match "([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12})") {
                $dbId = $matches[1]
                break
            }
        }
    }
} else {
    Write-Host "       Creating new database..." -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    $createOutput = npx wrangler d1 create raymond-db 2>&1 | Out-String
    Write-Host $createOutput -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    if ($createOutput -match "([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12})") {
        $dbId = $matches[1]
    }
}

if (-not $dbId) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "ERROR: Could not determine database ID." -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "Please run:  npx wrangler d1 list" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "Then copy the database_id for 'raymond-db' into wrangler.jsonc manually." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    exit 1
}

Write-Host "       Database ID: $dbId" -ForegroundColor Green

# -- Update wrangler.jsonc with the real DB ID
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "[5/7] Updating wrangler.jsonc with database ID..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$wranglerContent = Get-Content "wrangler.jsonc" -Raw
$wranglerContent = $wranglerContent -replace '"database_id"\s*:\s*"[^"]*"', "`"database_id`": `"$dbId`""
Set-Content -Path "wrangler.jsonc" -Value $wranglerContent -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "       wrangler.jsonc updated." -ForegroundColor Green

# -- Apply schema to remote database
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "[6/7] Applying database schema..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
npx wrangler d1 execute raymond-db --remote --file=./schema.sql
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "WARNING: Schema apply failed. You may need to run it manually later:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "         npx wrangler d1 execute raymond-db --remote --file=./schema.sql" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
} else {
    Write-Host "       Schema applied." -ForegroundColor Green
}

npm run build

مشکل از BOM (بایت اول فایل) هست که PowerShell موقع ساخت package.json اضافه کرده. Vite نمی‌تونه JSON رو بخونه.

یه دستور کوتاه این رو درست می‌کنه.

این رو بزن:
powershell
$files = @("package.json", "tsconfig.json", "wrangler.jsonc")
foreach ($f in $files) {
    if (Test-Path $f) {
        $content = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path $f))
        $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false
        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Resolve-Path $f), $content, $utf8NoBom)
        Write-Host "Fixed: $f" -ForegroundColor Green
    }
}

powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path . -Recurse -Include *.json,*.jsonc,*.ts,*.tsx,*.css,*.sql,*.md,*.html -File | Where-Object { $_.FullName -notmatch "node_modules|dist|\.wrangler" } | ForEach-Object {
    $content = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($_.FullName)
    $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($_.FullName, $content, $utf8NoBom)
}
Write-Host "All files cleaned." -ForegroundColor Green

اگه AI جواب داده بود، اینجا ۲ تا پیام می‌بینی (user + assistant).

مرحله ۳: لاگ Worker رو ببین
توی PowerShell، این رو بزن:

powershell
npx wrangler tail
این لاگ‌های زنده Worker رو نشون می‌ده. حالا توی مرورگر یه پیام جدید بفرست.

توی PowerShell باید ببینی چه اتفاقی می‌افته — خطا، موفقیت، یا هیچی.

وقتی تموم شد، Ctrl+C بزن تا از tail خارج شی.

حدس من
اگه همه‌چیز درست باشه ولی جواب نده، معمولاً یکی از ایناست:

۱. Workers AI توی اکانت تو فعال نیست
اولین بار که env.AI.run() رو صدا می‌زنی، Cloudflare باید Workers AI رو برای اکانتت فعال کنه. اگه ایمیل هنوز کامل تأیید نشده یا اکانت جدیده، ممکنه سکوت کنه.

راه‌حل: برو dash.cloudflare.com → Workers & Pages → AI → اگه صفحه‌ای باز شد که «Accept terms» داشت، قبول کن.

۲. مدل در دسترس نیست
مدل @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct ممکنه توی بعضی regionها در دسترس نباشه.

۳. JSON response خالیه
ممکنه env.AI.run() برگرده ولی محتوای خالی بده.

کل خروجی tail رو کپی کن و برام بفرست. اگه هیچی نشون نداد هم بگو.

نکته مهم
ممکنه مشکل این باشه که event bus درخواست رو async می‌فرسته با void this.deliver(...)، و Worker قبل از اینکه دیتابیس پیام رو ذخیره کنه بسته می‌شه. این یه باگ رایجه.

اگه لاگ‌ها این رو نشون بدن، فایل event-bus.ts رو یه کم تغییر می‌دیم:

void this.deliver(...) رو به await this.deliver(...) تبدیل می‌کنیم

یا از ctx.waitUntil() استفاده می‌کنیم

ولی اول لاگ رو ببینیم تا مطمئن شیم. tail رو بزن، پیام بفرست، لاگ رو برام کپی کن.

خب، این خیلی گویاست. درخواست POST /messages اصلاً به Worker نرسیده. فقط GET‌ها رو می‌بینم (که پولینگ UI هست). یعنی از مرورگر پیام فرستادی ولی POST هیچ‌وقت اجرا نشده.

دو تا احتمال:

۱. توی UI یه خطا رخ داده قبل از اینکه POST بفرسته (مثلاً createConversation خطا داده و هیچ‌وقت send نشده)

۲. یا اصلاً دکمه send رو نزدی و فقط صفحه باز موند و UI در حال polling بود (که همین رو نشون می‌ده — هر ۲ ثانیه یه GET)

راه‌حل مستقیم: از PowerShell خودمون POST رو تست کنیم
توی همون پنجره‌ای که tail روشنه، Ctrl+C بزن تا متوقف شه.

بعد این رو بزن:

powershell
$headers = @{ "Content-Type" = "application/json" }
$body = '{"content":"Hello from PowerShell"}'
